hints: Use polynomial long division, matching the leading term of \(2x^2-x+1\) to the current leading term of the dividend.
After each quotient term, multiply the whole divisor by that term and subtract before continuing.
When the remaining polynomial has degree below 2, record it separately as the remainder and check dividend = divisor × quotient + remainder.
walkthrough:
State the given polynomial division problem:
$$\text{Dividend} = 6x^4 + x^3 - x^2 + 5x - 6, \quad \text{Divisor} = 2x^2 - x + 1$$

Divide the leading term of the dividend by the leading term of the divisor to determine the first term of the quotient:
$$\dfrac{6x^4}{2x^2} = 3x^2$$

Multiply the entire divisor by $3x^2$:
$$3x^2(2x^2 - x + 1) = 6x^4 - 3x^3 + 3x^2$$

Divide the leading term of the new remainder by the leading term of the divisor to get the second term of the quotient:
$$\dfrac{4x^3}{2x^2} = +2x$$

Multiply the entire divisor by $2x$:
$$2x(2x^2 - x + 1) = 4x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x$$

Subtract this product from the current remainder:
$$(4x^3 - 4x^2 + 5x - 6) - (4x^3 - 2x^2 + 2x) = (-4 - (-2))x^2 + (5 - 2)x - 6$$
$$= -2x^2 + 3x - 6$$

Divide the leading term of the current remainder by the leading term of the divisor to get the third term of the quotient:
$$\dfrac{-2x^2}{2x^2} = -1$$

Multiply the entire divisor by $-1$:
$$-1(2x^2 - x + 1) = -2x^2 + x - 1$$

Subtract this product from the current remainder to obtain the final remainder:
$$(-2x^2 + 3x - 6) - (-2x^2 + x - 1) = (3 - 1)x + (-6 - (-1)) = 2x - 5$$
Since the remainder $2x - 5$ has degree $1$, which is strictly less than the degree of the divisor $2x^2 - x + 1$ (degree $2$), the polynomial division is complete.

State the quotient and remainder:
$$\text{Quotient} = 3x^2 + 2x - 1, \quad \text{Remainder} = 2x - 5$$
This satisfies the algebraic identity:
$$6x^4 + x^3 - x^2 + 5x - 6 = (2x^2 - x + 1)(3x^2 + 2x - 1) + (2x - 5)$$
